title: Console Walkthrough: Usage Analytics, Per-route Dashboards & Cost Breakdown - Solaris Health
summary: Redwood team walked Solaris through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Focus on per-route chargebacks, token-level cost attribution, alerts for cost anomalies, and how to map model/route configs to billing. Customer asked about data residency, SOC2 artifacts, and dedicated capacity pricing. Agreed next steps: share pricing and benchmark spreadsheet, export sample dashboard, and schedule a POC benchmark run in their staging environment.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing and pricing
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-07 14:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex, Priya, Janelle, Luis (Redwood) -- Maya, David, Rosa, Samir (Solaris)

[00:00] Alex: hey everybody, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. um, we'll do a 40 minute run through of the console, focus on usage analytics and then dig into per-route cost breakout. priya and janelle will demo, luis will cover the onboarding bits, and i'll handle next steps. maya, you mentioned a couple of items in the email, anything to add?

[00:18] Maya: thanks alex, yeah main things for us are 1) how we attribute cost to product teams per route, 2) how to detect and alert on cost spikes, and 3) what logs and audit data we can get for compliance. also we'll want a sense of dedicated capacity pricing if we need predictable throughput.

[00:35] Alex: perfect, that's what we'll target. priya, take it away.

[00:38] Priya: cool, starting in the console landing page, you'll see the usage overview. top-level is tokens consumed, requests per minute, and error rate. notice the shaded bands - those are the retention window and the time range selector, you can compare last 7 days vs last 30. the left panel filters by team, route, model, and deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private).

[01:10] David: is that live for our account yet or demo data?

[01:13] Priya: demo data for now, but same data model as your account. the filters map to your routes, so once connected your product routes will appear.

[01:26] Priya: jumping to per-route dashboards - select a route, 'patient-notes-summarize' in this example, and you'll get a breakdown: throughput, mean latency, tail latency p95/p99, tokens in/out, and cost attribution. cost attribution is computed from per-token model cost plus infra multiplier when dedicated.

[01:50] Rosa: how do you compute the infra multiplier? we run GPUs and need to reconcile with our internal chargeback.

[01:56] Priya: good question, the infra multiplier is configurable per deployment pool. you can set a fixed per-hour cost for a dedicated pool or use model-based unit costs for hosted. the console multiplies token usage by model unit cost and then adds pool overhead if dedicated - we also expose the raw components so you can use the numbers in your internal system.

[02:20] Samir: can you export per-route cost to CSV or connect to our finance bill?

[02:24] Janelle: yes, exports are available; there's a schedule export feature and a billing API endpoint. we'll share the sample CSV and the export template after.

[02:37] Alex: quick note, we also have tagging. if you tag requests client-side with team_id or project_id, the console will slice by tag and map cost automatically.

[02:50] Maya: that's promising. about anomaly detection - how do you detect cost spikes vs normal traffic spikes?

[02:56] Priya: two parts: statistical baselining for usage and an alerting engine. you set thresholds on tokens, requests, or cost per route. we also provide anomaly alerts that use a rolling baseline and flag deviations. alerts can be sent to Slack, email, or webhook.

[03:20] David: what's the granularity of the data? minute level? second?

[03:24] Priya: we store raw request-level metadata for 30 days by default, aggregated metrics at 1-minute granularity for 90 days and daily summaries for 13 months. retention windows adjustable per plan.

[03:40] Rosa: and audit logs for regulatory purposes?

[03:44] Luis: yes, audit logs include request metadata, who changed route configs, and model version rollouts. for Private deployments we can integrate with your SIEM and push logs to your S3 or Splunk.

[03:58] Priya: showing a per-route trace now - you can click a request to see prompt/response length, model used, latency breakdown, and cost calc. note: transcripts in this demo are redacted, in your environment we do not store full prompt text without explicit config due to PII concerns.

[04:21] Samir: you mentioned token-level cost - does that account for quantized models or different compute footprints?

[04:28] Priya: yes, the unit cost is model-specific and we maintain a model catalog. for quantized or lower precision variants we have separate unit costs; when a route is configured to fallback to a quantized variant the console attributes cost to the actual model used.

[04:45] Maya: how do rollouts show up? if we canary a new model, can we see cost differences between canary and baseline?

[04:51] Janelle: absolutely - rollouts show split by cohort, and the per-route dashboard has a segment for each variant. you can compare quality metrics and cost side-by-side. we also surface regression alerts tied to eval sets if you enable it.

[05:10] Alex: quick detour on competitors - several customers ask about Anthropic and OpenAI. keep in mind our console focuses on per-route economics and dedicated routing which they don't all expose in the same way.

[05:27] Maya: yes we've been looking at prod tradeoffs with OpenAI for hosted and infra for private. do you support bringing your own model via S3 or gcs?

[05:35] Priya: in Private deployments yes, you can onboard customer models; for hosted we curate the catalog but can add verified customer models under an enterprise agreement.

[05:48] David: can we map routes to our internal cost centers automatically? we use a cost center code on every request header.

[05:56] Janelle: that's ideal - if you send cost_center as a request header tag, the console will map to that and you can create saved views and scheduled exports per cost center.

[06:10] Priya: demoing alert config now - create alert, condition = token volume > baseline*2 for 15 minutes, notify Slack channel #infra-costs, severity = high. you can add suppression windows to avoid noisy alerts during deployments.

[06:35] Rosa: on Slack integration - we need to limit who sees cost numbers. RBAC?

[06:40] Luis: we support role-based access controls, SSO via SAML, and team-scoped views. cost dashboards can be restricted to finance role or team leads. audit logs record who viewed exports.

[06:58] Maya: good. what's typical accuracy of cost attribution? any edge cases to watch for?

[07:04] Priya: attribution is exact for model token usage; infra overhead is based on configured pool usage. edge cases are shared infrastructure where you host multiple tenants on the same GPUs - we recommend dedicated pools for strict chargeback.

[07:20] Samir: show me the cost breakdown screen please.

[07:22] Priya: clicking cost breakdown - top of page is high-level $/day, then per-model and per-route buckets. below that we show model unit cost, tokens used, infra overhead, and 3rd party license fees if any. each line item is clickable to see the raw request list.

[07:45] David: is there a way to simulate cost if we change batch sizes or enable kv caching?

[07:50] Janelle: yes we have an optimizer simulation tool - you can change batching, caching, and quantization toggles and it projects cost delta based on your historical usage profile. we'll share a link to the Optimize runbook and sample simulations.

[08:10] Maya: this is helpful. can we run a POC with our staging traffic to validate those projections?

[08:15] Alex: yes, typical next step is a POC. we'll run a benchmark with a subset of your staging traffic, measure latency, cost, and KV cache hit rates. priya, can we propose timeline?

[08:25] Priya: we can start next week, 1 week of baseline capture then 2 weeks of optimization testing. requires a staging key and a list of routes. estimate ~3 weeks total.

[08:36] Maya: Rosa, any blockers from security?

[08:39] Rosa: need SOC2 report and KMS integration details. also need to know if logs can be redacted and if transcripts can be prevented from being stored.

[08:47] Luis: we will share SOC2 Type II and the KMS/HSM integration doc. redaction settings are configurable; by default prompt/response are not persisted unless you turn on session storage. for Private you keep everything inside your VPC.

[09:05] Samir: ok good. show us an example scheduled export and a sample CSV.

[09:09] Janelle: exporting - CSV columns: date, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_cost, infra_overhead, total_cost, team_tag. sample export link: placeholder link to sample CSV (we will attach after call).

[09:30] Priya: walking through saved views and dashboards - you can pin a per-route dashboard, share with specific users, and schedule it as a daily delivery to email.

[09:45] David: how granular are the model cost numbers; e.g., different context lengths?

[09:50] Priya: cost is calculated per request using actual tokens in/out, so long context length shows up proportionally in tokens. we also expose estimated tokenization differences across languages.

[10:05] Maya: on dedicated pricing, do you have example tiers?

[10:09] Alex: yes typical tiers: small pool (2x A100 equiv) for pilots, medium (8x) for product teams, large (32x) for high throughput. pricing depends on reserved hours and support tier. we'll send a tailored quote.

[10:25] Rosa: if we want to keep data in region EU, do you support it?

[10:29] Luis: yes, we have region pinning and private deployments in EU regions. for enterprise we can set data residency constraints and ensure logs remain in-region.

[10:42] Priya: switching to anomaly detection examples - here's a spike where a route had a model fallback which increased cost; alert triggered and we show the exact requests that fellback. you can set automated rollback policies on rollout configs.

[11:05] Samir: show me the rollback policy config.

[11:08] Priya: here - policy name, condition, action; e.g., if cost delta > 20% and p95 latency > 200ms then revert to previous variant. can wire to Kubernetes rollout or just route config.

[11:30] Maya: nice. can we add custom metrics from our side to the console?

[11:35] Janelle: yes, you can send custom metrics via our metrics API and map them to dashboards. common usage is to send quality metrics from your eval harness.

[11:50] David: any limits on request tags or headers?

[11:54] Priya: tags are strings up to 128 chars, and you can send up to 10 custom tags per request.

[12:05] Rosa: security question - how long do you keep full request metadata in hosted vs private?

[12:10] Luis: hosted defaults: request metadata 30 days, aggregated metrics 13 months. for enterprise plans retention is configurable. for Private you control retention. we can provide contract language for retention limits.

[12:30] Alex: wrapping toward next steps - i'll summarize.

[12:34] Alex: action items: we'll share SOC2, KMS doc, pricing, sample CSV, and benchmark plan. you will provide staging key, list of routes, and the teams to tag for cost centers.

[12:47] Maya: timeline - if we start next week POC, we hope to have results in 3 weeks. security signoff needed by Rosa.

[12:56] Samir: any blockers on our side? looks fine.

[13:00] Alex: great. janelle, anything else to show?

[13:04] Janelle: quick note, we have a prebuilt Optimize template for retail/health customers that already includes caching and batching presets. we'll attach that.

[13:16] David: thanks all, can we get the scheduled export example and pricing by Thursday?

[13:21] Alex: yes, we'll send by Thursday 2026-12-10.

[13:24] Luis: i'll follow up with the onboarding doc and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.

[13:30] Maya: thanks everyone, this was useful.

[13:33] Alex: thanks all, we'll wrap.

End of call
